name: _to_sparse_semi_structured
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_to_sparse_semi_structured(Tensor dense) -> (Tensor, Tensor). Original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract; do not narrow tests to this signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::_to_sparse_semi_structured(Tensor dense) -> (Tensor, Tensor). Semantics: takes a 2-D dense Tensor of a supported dtype (float16/bfloat16, int8, float32; bfloat16 only where the device supports it) and returns exactly two tensors: a compressed/"packed" payload tensor and a metadata tensor, both on the same device as the input. In every successful tested row the dense input still equals its reference copy after the call, and the schema lists no mutated arguments with empty alias annotations on both returns; that alias annotation is representative schema metadata rather than a tested runtime guarantee, and the pytest does not exercise output aliasing. The dtype-dependent alignment geometry and retained-slot groups recorded by the pytest describe the measured behavior of the target build (float16/bfloat16 rows % 32 and columns % 32; int8 rows % 16 and columns % 64; float32 rows % 32 and columns % 16; retained-slot group 2:4 for 16-bit/int8 and 1:2 for float32), not a claim that every backend or version behaves identically. The pytest file owns the full behavioral surface: shape/empty/pattern/layout (transposed, sliced, expanded, dilated) and special-value (nan/inf) families must match the two-tensor ATen result with zero tolerance, non-contiguous views must preserve parent storage, strides and offset, and RuntimeError is expected for invalid rank, misaligned geometry, under-/over-filled sparsity patterns and unsupported dtypes. This definition records only the single registered 'default' overload; it does not express conditional, dtype- or shape-dependent error and mutation behavior, which remains in the original Gems pytest.
